This change alters the conceptual understanding of suffering from a state of enduring to one of opposing.
column7: Suffering is the endurance of pain-physical, emotional, mental, or spiritual-especially when prolonged or intense.
column8: Suffering is the resistance to pain - physical, emotional, mental, or spiritual - especially when it is prolonged or intense.

column6: Both paragraphs convey the same core idea about human adaptability and the distinction between the capacity to change and the willingness to change, with only slight variations in wording.
column7: Man has great capacity to change; it's wired into our very essence. Humans are very adaptable, we can learn and grow, and find better ways to do things. However, a capacity to change is not the same as a willingness or a persuasion to change.
column8: Human beings have a great capacity for change; it is built into our very essence. We humans are highly adaptable, we can learn and grow, and find better ways to do things. However, the ability to change is not the same as the willingness or the conviction to change.
